What Photoshop Content Credentials reveal about your edits — and how to remove them

Exported a design and worried your client will see your messy process? Here is what Photoshop’s Content Credentials and edit log actually store, what you can control inside Photoshop, and how to check and clean the exported file.

Updated 2026-11-26 · 6 min read
Short answer: No. Content Credentials store a summary of edit types — “colour adjustments”, “cropped”, “placed another image” — not every step. They can also include the app, your name or connected accounts, the images you placed and whether you used generative AI. You can’t hide single edits: you can turn off whole categories or the feature in Photoshop, or remove the credentials from the exported file with IA Cleaner.

What Photoshop can store in an exported image

  • Content Credentials (C2PA): when the feature is on, the export carries a signed record with the app and version, optionally your name or connected accounts, and a list of actions such as “opened”, “colour adjustments”, “cropped”, “placed another image”, “resized” or “drawing”.
  • Ingredients: if you placed other images, the record can list them as ingredients, sometimes with small thumbnails.
  • Generative AI use: when you use Firefly features such as Generative Fill, Adobe adds Content Credentials saying AI was used, even if you never turned the feature on yourself.
  • XMP history: separately, Photoshop writes a short history of saves into XMP, and if you enabled the History Log in Preferences it can write a detailed list of steps into the file’s metadata.

Does it show every edit you made?

Not every brush stroke. Content Credentials store a summary of action types — you will see “colour adjustments ×3”, not each curve you tried. But that summary, plus the list of placed files and the AI flag, is often enough to tell how an image was built.

The detailed step-by-step list only appears if the History Log is set to save to metadata. That one can be very explicit, so check it.

Can you hide some edits and keep others?

Not individually. Inside Photoshop you can turn Content Credentials on or off and choose which categories of information to include (for example producer, edits and activity, connected accounts) before exporting. You can’t pick single edits to hide. If you want to keep nothing, export without Content Credentials or clean the exported copy.

See what your file reveals, then clean it

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Images and drop the exported JPG, PNG or WebP.
  2. Read the box What the original reveals about how it was made: the tool, the author or account, AI use and the edit history from Content Credentials and XMP.
  3. Click Download clean image. The clean copy keeps every pixel and the colour profile, and none of that history.

The file is processed in your browser and never uploaded, so it is safe for client work.

Settings to check in Photoshop

  • Content Credentials panel (Window → Content Credentials): turn it off, or untick what you don’t want to include.
  • History Log (Preferences → History Log, or History & Content Credentials in recent versions): don’t save log items to metadata.
  • Export As / Save for Web: set Metadata to None or Copyright only.

Remember that the PSD itself keeps all layers and history. Send a flattened export, not the working file.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) it identifies and removes GPS location, camera and phone model, dates, editing apps, XMP and IPTC data, C2PA Content Credentials and embedded AI prompts. Pixels and colour profile stay the same. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
